per_option_rationale.rationale: Student substitutes x = 3 directly into the numerator: 9 - 9 = 0, ignoring that the denominator is also 0 and the limit must be found by factoring.
Student reports x = 3 as the answer, equating the limit point with the limit value.
Student evaluates x² at x = 3 and reports 9, substituting into only part of the expression.

explanation: Direct substitution gives 0/0. Factor the numerator: x² - 9 = (x - 3)(x + 3). Cancel the common factor (x - 3) to get lim(x -> 3)(x + 3) = 3 + 3 = 6.

explanation_sections.punchline: Direct substitution produces 0/0. Factor the numerator as (x - 3)(x + 3), cancel the common (x - 3), then substitute x = 3 to get 6.
explanation_sections.approach: When a limit gives 0/0, do not stop. Factor the numerator using the difference-of-squares or other identities. Cancel the common factor with the denominator. Only then substitute the limit value. This is the standard technique for removable discontinuities.
explanation_sections.lesson: A 0/0 form at a point does not mean the limit is 0. Factor and cancel first, then substitute. The limit may be a finite nonzero number.
explanation_sections.timing: About 90 seconds. Identifying the 0/0 form takes 10 seconds. Factoring x² - 9 takes 15 seconds. The rest is substitution. Do not waste time trying L'Hopital at this level.
